t: That this Act may be cited as the “Federal Metal and Nonmetallic Mine Safety Act”.

fable.w: This section only gives the Act its short title, the "Federal Metal and Nonmetallic Mine Safety Act". The tempting reading is that a mine safety statute implies consultation with operators, states, or advisory committees, but nothing in this section creates any such process. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision here.

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard short title provision. It merely establishes the name by which the Act is known and does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government.
qwen_block.s: That this Act may be cited as the “Federal Metal and Nonmetallic Mine Safety Act”.

opus.w: This section only gives the Act its short title, the "Federal Metal and Nonmetallic Mine Safety Act." It creates no process that brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision. A regulatory-sounding title is not enough to show participation.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking:** The only possible pull is that the title names a mine safety law, and such laws often include hearings or rulemaking. That doesn't hold up. This section is just the short title. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue, and it involves no one outside the federal government.
